prompt: A ladder leans against a wall at a $65^\circ$ angle with the ground and touches the wall $12$ ft above the ground. How long is the ladder, in feet, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: Label the sides relative to the $65^\circ$ angle at the ground. Notice that this time the unknown is the longest side.

hints.text: Label the sides relative to the $65^\circ$ angle at the ground. Notice that this time the unknown is the longest side.
The $12$ ft height is opposite and the ladder $L$ is the hypotenuse, so $\sin 65^\circ = \frac{12}{L}$. Rearrange to $L = \frac{12}{\sin 65^\circ}$.
$L = \frac{12}{\sin 65^\circ} \approx \frac{12}{0.9063} \approx 13.2$, so the ladder is about $13.2$ feet long.

explanation: The height of $12$ feet is opposite the $65^\circ$ angle and the ladder $L$ is the hypotenuse, so sine is the ratio that links them.
Writing $\sin 65^\circ = \frac{12}{L}$ and multiplying by $L$, then dividing by $\sin 65^\circ$, gives $L = \frac{12}{\sin 65^\circ}$.
Evaluating gives $L \approx \frac{12}{0.9063} \approx 13.2$, so the ladder is about $13.2$ feet long.

alternativeExplanations.title: The hypotenuse is always biggest
steps: Whatever you compute, the ladder must be longer than the $12$ ft it reaches up the wall.
$13.2 > 12$ ✓. If you had multiplied instead of divided you would have gotten $10.9$ ft — shorter than the wall height, which is impossible.
